_comment: STAIR TEST RIG (owner-designed, 2026-08-07). NOT CONTENT - a diagnostic fixture. Its only job is to isolate the multi-level traversal defect: after wiring the StairConnector prefabs the bake still reports PathPartial on every multi-level dungeon, and hunting that through dg_bonecrypt's 21 rooms and 4 stair pairs is a way to spend twenty minutes learning what four rooms would show. So this chains ONE FLAT ROOM between every stair pair and contains NOTHING ELSE - no encounters, no traps, no chests, no keys, no locks. Anything that fails to path here is the stairs, because there is nothing else it could be. Walk it top to bottom; the first descent you cannot make names the variant that is broken. Owner hand-edits the connector prefabs, hands the offsets back, and they are folded into DefaultStairConnectorRoomsBuilder - the SCRIPT stays the source of truth, the prefabs are never the authority (BuildAll overwrites Assets/Dungeon/Rooms).
_variants: Each pair names its connector prefab DIRECTLY rather than the StairDown/StairUp archetype, so the rig tests all three shapes. The baker's alias (StairDown -> StairConnector_Vertical_Down) only covers the archetype path; naming a concrete stem bypasses it, which is exactly what the alias's own note says self-retires once the composer emits concrete stems.
_knownIssue: Left/Right land 0.80m clear of the wall against a 1.00m minimum walkable slot (2 x agentRadius 0.5), so navmesh erosion removes their top landing and they are EXPECTED to fail until TurnRun 4.0 -> 3.5 lands. Vertical lands 1.30m clear and is the one that should work. If Vertical also fails, the defect is not the landing width.
